issue_request: FHIR-14389 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked to fix ElementDefinition invariant eld-16 so the sliceName regular expression allows the literal @default slice name reserved by the profiling rules.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 116056cc35dadc8649cab84578377258a304b857, whose message says "GF#14389 - fix eld-16" and whose svn revision 13366 matches the Jira comment. That commit added @ to both the FHIRPath and XPath forms of the eld-16 sliceName regex in source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini keeps ElementDefinition in the active datatype build inputs, and the current profiling and ElementDefinition narrative still describe @default as the reserved default-slice name. Other eld-16 Jira issues in the same family dealt with slash, bracket, and regex-escaping details; the current regex preserves those characters and @. The later STU3 technical-correction request FHIR-25776 was resolved no-change and does not require a current core source edit.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative ElementDefinition spreadsheet source already contains @ in the eld-16 regex, and the surrounding current narrative remains consistent with the Jira request.
